 The Hawaii Rainbow Warriors (2-0) face the UT Arlington Mavericks (2-0) on November 8, 2026.
 In its previous game, Hawaii topped Bethesda (CA) on Saturday, 116-44. Zack Davidson scored a team-high 20 points (and contributed two assists and nine rebounds). UT Arlington was victorious in its previous game versus Portland, 89-85, on Friday. Teodor Simic starred with 24 points, and also had five boards and zero assists.
 When is Hawaii vs. UT Arlington and when does it start?
 This matchup between the Rainbow Warriors and Mavericks is set to start on Sunday, November 8, 2026. You can expect the opening tip at 10 p.m. ET.
 Where to Watch Hawaii vs. UT Arlington
 The Rainbow Warriors and Mavericks will take to the court at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center for this matchup on Nov. 8, and if you want to catch the game live, get your tickets now from Vivid Seats ! 
 What channel is the game on?
 You can catch this game live on MW+.
 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors vs. UT Arlington Mavericks Game Preview
 Hawaii Stats, Odds & Insights (2025-26)
 Hawaii was 86th in the nation in points scored (79.6 per game) and 78th in points allowed (70.5) last year.
 Last year, the Rainbow Warriors recorded 79.6 points per game, 12.9 more points than the 66.7 the Mavericks allowed.
 Hawaii was 199th in college basketball in 3-pointers made (7.5 per game) and 310th in 3-point percentage (31.6%) last year.
 The Rainbow Warriors averaged 81.7 points per game last year at home, which was 4.8 more points than they averaged in away games (76.9).
 UT Arlington Stats, Odds & Insights (2025-26)
 UT Arlington was lifted by its defense last season, as it ranked 24th-best in the nation by giving up only 66.7 points per game. It ranked 308th in college basketball in points scored (70 per contest).
 The Mavericks put up an average of 70 points per game last year, only 0.5 fewer points than the 70.5 the Rainbow Warriors gave up.
 When it came to threes, UT Arlington struggled, as it ranked 0-worst in college basketball in treys made (4.9 per game) and 0-worst in three-point percentage (29.1%). 
 The Mavericks put up more points at home (74.4 per game) than away (67) last season.
